_README: TRANCHE 13 - R1. One body, no params, no blanks, no heading.
ANSWERING YOUR SCHEMA QUESTION FIRST, because it changes what this tranche contains.
You asked whether the seed needs a marker for 'a position with one body plus a table-emission
behaviour'. My answer: NO - because that is not the shape. R1 is an ordinary one-body position.
The table is not R1's behaviour. It is the SKELETON's.
This follows directly from B4. Headings are template-owned: the skeleton supplies them, bodies
never carry them, and a position does not 'have heading-emission behaviour'. Paras 51-59 are
the same kind of thing one level up - a fixed run of template paragraphs that the assembler
replaces with engine-supplied rows. They are owned by the skeleton, they exist whether or not
R1 is the selected rung, and there is no canonical body behind them at all. Contract E already
says the rows are precomputed and the assembler does zero math; this just says WHERE the rows
land, and the answer is a skeleton paragraph range, not a position field.
So the thing that needs loader support is a MANIFEST CATEGORY, not a seed marker:
category `computed_table` - emitted; carries no canonical body; rule-2 exempt exactly as
`heading` and `letter_shell` are; content supplied by the engine at assembly time. Paras
51-59 collapse to one such entry (or nine, if you would rather keep the index space
paragraph-per-paragraph - your call, the manifest is yours).
Why this is the better place for it:
- If the marker lived on the position, then R0 - a different rung of the same clause -
would need its own copy of the same marker, and so would any future rung. The table is
invariant across rungs; the rungs are not.
- Rule 4 reverse coverage stays honest. A skeleton category is something rule 2 knows to
skip. A position field is something rule 4 would have to be taught to interpret.
- It keeps 'position -> body' total. Every position has bodies and nothing else. The moment
one position carries a behaviour flag, every consumer has to ask whether the flag is set
before it can trust the body list.
If you disagree, the fallback I would accept is an explicit position field you define and the
loader validates - never a field I invent that the loader ignores. But I do not think you need
one, and this tranche is written on the assumption that you don't: R1 below has no marker of
any kind.
PARA 61 - the body. Template markers '[{R1}' and ']' stripped. Nothing else changed.
No heading (B4). No params: every noun in it is either fixed or resolved by the engine.
'Landlord's estimate' is not a blank - the sentence is about the estimate, not filled with it.
EXPLICITLY NOT BODY TEXT, and worth stating because each looks like it should be:
paras 51-59  - the tab-delimited rent rows. Placeholder for the computed table, above.
para 49      - instruction marker. Guidance, never emitted.
paras 36-47  - the R0 block. R0 is registered in loi_deferred_position and stays deferred.
Do NOT let this tranche flip the `rent` clause active in a way that lets R0
go silently absent - that is precisely the failure test P3 guards.
ACCEPTANCE TEST CONSEQUENCE, already agreed but restating so it is in one place with the
tranche that causes it: Powder Springs OMITTED this sentence. All three sent LOIs did. It is
in the 'Provision in LOI' block of both handbook editions and is tenant-protective, so we
emit it deliberately. That is expected diff #2 alongside SALE OF PROPERTY stripping.

_note: Nothing superseded. `rent`/R1/main is a NEW body - the rent clause had no loaded
body at all, which is why it was registered deferred.

clauses.guidance_note: SHAPE = SELECTOR, NOT A RANKED LADDER. R0 and R1 are not preferences - neither is 'better' and nobody negotiates from one to the other; which applies is a DEAL FACT. Same axis the CAM incident resolved when building_type was retired for cam_basis. R0 is not loaded, so the variant declares subdomain {per_sqft} and is valid with R1 alone - the same mechanism that lets the ECDT CAM variant be valid with CAM0 alone. R0 later arrives in its own variant declaring {annual}: no re-ranking, no re-keying of R1.
